subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should manual `openclaw cron run` be accepted as a non-consuming verification path that never drives `deleteAfterRun`, retry/backoff, counters, or failure-alert state, with `lastRunWasManual` exposed in cron state?
rationale: The patch is a coherent bug fix, but it deliberately changes persisted cron state semantics and notification behavior that existing operators may have come to rely on.

options.title: Accept non-consuming manual runs
options.body: Merge after maintainers confirm the policy and ensure release notes explain that manual runs preserve scheduled delete/retry/backoff/alert state.

options.title: Narrow the behavior change
options.body: Revise the PR to preserve only the destructive `deleteAfterRun` guard while keeping some existing manual counter or alert behavior if that is the intended compatibility contract.

options.title: Pause for separate cron policy design
options.body: Keep the branch open or close it in favor of a maintainer-authored cron manual-run policy if the public `lastRunWasManual` state is not the desired contract.

recommendation.title: Accept non-consuming manual runs
recommendation.body: Merge after maintainers confirm the policy and ensure release notes explain that manual runs preserve scheduled delete/retry/backoff/alert state.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest sampled history across cron manual-run, persistence, and scheduling owner boundaries.
